title: Two majorities that never meet
request:
a cluster moving from {s1,s2,s3} to {s3,s4,s5}, and three sets of voters

./your_program.sh raft-membership
init ["s1","s2","s3"]
joint ["s3","s4","s5"]
agree ["s1","s2"]
agree ["s4","s5"]
agree ["s1","s2","s3","s4"]
note: {s1,s2} is a majority of the old configuration and {s4,s5} of the new, and the two sets are disjoint. Switch directly from C_old to C_new and both could elect a leader in the same term, which is the one thing Raft promises cannot happen. In the joint phase neither carries the decision, so neither can.

title: One change at a time
request:
two single-server additions, the second attempted before the first commits

./your_program.sh raft-membership
init ["s1","s2","s3"]
add s4
state
add s5
commit-change
add s5
state
note: A single-server change is safe on its own because the old and new majorities always overlap — three of four still contains two of three. Two overlapping changes give that up: {s1,s2,s3} to {s1,s2,s3,s4} to {s1,s2,s3,s4,s5} has {s1,s2} deciding for the first and {s3,s4,s5} for the last, and they are disjoint again.
